caption: The drawing is a black and white, top-down architectural plan labeled "THE GARDEN OF THOMAS C. VEITCH" and "THE BLACKWELL SURVEY." The composition is centered around a large, rectangular building with a defined roof structure and symmetrical wings. Surrounding the building are geometric and organic shapes representing different types of landscaping, including various paths, circular and square garden beds, and grouped tree symbols. Above the building, curved paths enclose tree-lined areas, symmetric rows, and a segmented arched section filled with trees at the top of the image. To the left of the building, there are small circular and rectangular features, some containing clustered dots denoting bushes or trees. On the right, patterns of small repeating squares or dots suggest planting beds or orchards. Below the building, there are three main zones: a rectangular tennis court to the left, an ornate circular and curvilinear garden pattern at the center with several intersecting walkways, and a section of systematically arranged rectangular beds to the right. All lines are rendered in contrasting black and off-white or light beige, creating clear borders and solid fills throughout the plan.
title: Garden of Thomas Veitch
